title: AI Coding Assistants in 2026: Who Should Pay
body_md: ![github.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/ai-coding-assistants-in-2026-who-should-pay/1.png) *Screenshot of github.com ([source](https://github.com/features/copilot/plans))* **My verdict:** If you write code most workdays, exactly one of these is worth paying for — and for most people it's the $10 or $20 entry tier, not the $100–$200 one. GitHub Copilot Pro is the right default if you live in VS Code and want predictable billing. Cursor Pro is worth it if you actually want the editor to make multi-file changes for you. Claude Code is worth it if your work happens in a terminal. They are *not* worth paying for if you code occasionally, if you're still learning fundamentals, or if you expect a flat fee — because in 2026 almost none of these are flat fees anymore. I'm leading with that because the hard part this year isn't picking a tool, it's not getting surprised by the bill. ## What's Actually Going On ![docs.github.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/ai-coding-assistants-in-2026-who-should-pay/2.png) *Screenshot of docs.github.com ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-billing/models-and-pricing))* The three mainstream options have converged on the same shape: a cheap seat, plus metered AI usage on top. **GitHub Copilot.** Copilot is free for individuals with limits, $10 a month for Pro, $39 for Pro+, $100 for Max, $19 per seat for Business and $39 per seat for Enterprise. The free tier includes 2,000 monthly code completions and 50 premium requests a month. The important change this year is billing. On June 1, 2026, every Copilot plan moved to usage-based billing: GitHub retired premium requests and replaced them with GitHub AI Credits, billed by token consumption at each model's listed API rate, where 1 credit equals $0.01. Here's the part the original version of this post got wrong: the bundled credits don't match the sticker price, they exceed it. Pro's $10 buys 1,500 credits ($15 of usage), Pro+'s $39 buys 7,000 ($70), and Max's $100 buys 20,000 ($200). That's 1.5x on Pro, about 1.79x on Pro+, exactly 2x on Max. Max is sold on priority access to premium models and agents — sustained agent work is the only thing that burns $200 of credits. **Cursor.** A separate editor rather than a plugin. Plans are Hobby (free), Pro $20/mo, Pro+ $60/mo, Ultra $200/mo, plus Teams at $40/user/mo Standard or $120 Premium, with Enterprise custom. Pro includes $20 of model usage, Pro+ includes $70, and Ultra includes $400. Yearly billing takes 20% off — so Pro is $16/month annually and a Premium team seat is $96. The structure runs two pools: one for Cursor's own models and one for third-party frontier models, which draw usage at those providers' API rates. Since August 2026, even Auto mode is metered rather than priced as a flat house rate. **Claude Code.** Anthropic's terminal agent, sold as part of a Claude subscription rather than on its own. Pro is $20/month, or $17/month if you pay $200 up front for the year; Max is $100/month for 5x Pro's usage or $200/month for 20x, and Max is billed monthly only. Claude Code is included on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise, and it is not on the Free plan. You can also run it on pay-as-you-go API billing instead. A sourcing note, since this is a pricing post: these figures come from vendor documentation and from pricing trackers that cite the vendor pages. Credit-based plans move fast. Check the live page before you enter a card. ## Where It Breaks - **"Unlimited" means completions, not agents.** Autocomplete is effectively unlimited on paid tiers. The expensive part — a model reading your repo and editing ten files — is metered. Tab completions cost nothing; a handful of agent-mode tasks on a frontier model can run several dollars in credits. - **Overage is the real price.** Every paid Cursor tier bills against a pool of included model usage, so the sticker price is only the floor, and what you actually pay depends on how many frontier model requests you run. Set a spending cap on day one. - **Automation gets billed separately from your chats.** Anthropic's October 7, 2026 release notes announced monthly API credits of $100 on Max 5x and $200 on Max 20x. Those credits cover the Claude API, the Console Playground, Claude Managed Agents and the Claude Agent SDK — not interactive Claude Code in the terminal, IDE, desktop or web. Reporting has been inconsistent about whether Pro gets its own programmatic credit, so don't budget a CI pipeline around one without checking your account. - **A stray environment variable can move your spending.** If `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set on your machine, Claude Code bills that key at API rates instead of your plan. - **Availability isn't guaranteed at the top end.** Individual sign-ups were paused on April 20 when agentic workloads outran subscription pricing and have been reopening gradually since mid-June — so don't build a plan around the $100 tier without checking the plans page first. ## So Which One | You are | Pay for | Why | | --- | --- | --- | | In VS Code daily, want a boring bill | Copilot Pro, $10 | Cheapest serious seat; $10 buys $15 of credits | | Want the editor to do multi-file work | Cursor Pro, $20 | Agent-first editor, $20 usage pool included | | Working in the terminal / on servers | Claude Pro, $20 | Claude Code included at the lowest paid tier | | Running agents all day, every day | Copilot Max / Cursor Ultra | Where $100 buys $200 and $200 buys $400 of usage | | Coding a few hours a week | Nothing | Copilot Free's 2,000 completions will cover you | The $200 tiers are rational only if you've already blown through a $20 pool two months running. Buying one pre-emptively is paying for a habit you don't have yet. *Updated October 2026. This guide is based on vendor pricing and billing documentation plus pricing trackers that cite it — not on a controlled side-by-side test of the three tools.* ## My Take My read: the flat-fee era ended quietly and the headline prices are camouflage. Copilot Pro stayed at $10 a month, Pro+ at $39, Business at $19 per user and Enterprise at $39 per seat when usage billing arrived. That reads like stability. It isn't. Your bill now depends on how you work, not which plan you clicked. I think the generous-looking credit multipliers are the thing to watch, not the thing to celebrate. Doubling your money at Max only pays off if you reliably spend it, and a plan that hands you $200 of metered usage is a plan designed around people who will exceed it. Pro's 1.5x is the honest tier for most working developers. Cursor's August move to per-model metering is a bigger deal than the plan table suggests, because your cost now changes when the vendor changes routing. I think that's fair but uncomfortable, and I'd rather pay Copilot's slightly worse agent $10 for a predictable number than audit a model-routing bill every month. The fair point on the other side: if your agents genuinely save hours a week, per-model pricing is the cheaper structure, and Cursor's $400 pool at Ultra is the most usage anyone bundles. One thing I want to flag carefully — secondary sources report that Cursor's parent company was acquired in 2026. I could not confirm that on a vendor page, so treat it as unverified. I'd still weigh ownership stability before standardizing a 50-person team on any one editor. I'm not a financial or procurement professional and none of this is financial advice. But on cost the pattern is clear enough: start at $10 or $20, find the spending cap before you forget it exists, and let two months of actual overages — not a feature chart — decide whether you move up.
